words.Title: Flamefall Analytics
words.Subtitle: Flame in Freefall: what microgravity combustion experiments actually measured, for spacecraft fire safety.
words.One line: An interactive console over NASA's microgravity combustion data.
words.Hero number caption: droplet burns on the space station, one row each

title.source: NASA/TP-2015-216046, Table IX (FLEX-001 to FLEX-280). Totals recomputed from the table.

words.Title: Fire behaves differently in space, and the rules for stopping it were written for gravity.
words.Stakes: A fire in a crewed cabin or habitat has nowhere to go, and the crew cannot step outside.
words.Hero number caption: records returned by a search of NASA's PSI repository for “combustion”: the starting point of this console's catalogue

problem.source: PSI Data Repository, search “combustion”, retrieved 2026-11-14. 24 of the 26 records are combustion science; 2 are other research areas. The console adds 7 related investigations the search does not return.

words.Hero number caption: droplet burns, one row each in Table IX of NASA/TP-2015-216046
words.What it is: Single droplets of methanol or n-heptane burned on the space station while the atmosphere was varied.
words.Method: Every total here was recomputed from the table, not copied from the report's text.

words.Title: Fuel matters as much as atmosphere
words.Hero number caption: of all 276 tests ended with the visible flame going out
words.One line: Same apparatus, overlapping atmospheres, different fuel, very different outcome.
words.Chart label 2: SHARE ENDING IN EXTINCTION, BY OXYGEN LEVEL TESTED

fuel.source: NASA/TP-2015-216046, Table IX, recomputed from the data. Scatter: share of tests ending in Extinction at each tested oxygen level.

words.Title: “Extinction” only means the visible flame went out
words.Hero number caption: n-heptane “extinctions” show evidence that the droplet kept burning as a cool flame
words.Why it matters: A sensor that watches for visible flame will miss a cool flame. Gas cool flames burn at 600 to 1000 K.
words.Chart label: THE 60 N-HEPTANE TESTS LOGGED AS EXTINCTION

cool.source: NASA/TP-2015-216046, Appendix B figure captions. Cool-flame temperature, as reported for gas cool flames: University of Maryland Fire Protection Engineering news release, 2021.

words.Kicker: THE MODEL AND THE SCENARIO LAB
words.Hero number caption: headline AUC: the worse of grouped cross-validation (0.88) and leave-one-fuel-out (0.74). 0.5 is a coin flip, 1 is perfect.
words.What the model is: Three small logistic models, each trained on one kind of evidence and tested on unseen groups.
words.The honest line: 18% false-positive rate at the working threshold: 16 of 90 negatives called positive. One of three models fails; the console shows it.
words.Chart label 2: NEAREST REAL TESTS BY OXYGEN, PRESSURE AND FLOW SPEED

model.source: Model: scripts/train_models.py and data/models in the project's code (grouped cross-validation, seed 42), on NASA/TP-2015-216046, Table IX; FLEX-114 is left out: its pressure is printed as 0 mmHg and treated as missing. Nearest tests: NASA/TM-20210011385, Table A.1. Pressure taken as 1 atm.

words.Kicker: WHAT WE DON'T KNOW, AND WHERE TO LOOK
words.Title: A console that shows only what was measured would hide the most useful fact: where the measurements stop.
words.Hero number 1 caption: partial-gravity combustion tests in the PSI repository
words.Hero number 2 caption: highest oxygen of any solid-fuel test point with a stated outcome
words.Hero number 3 caption: droplet tests that contain both CO2 and helium
words.Cannot see:
cool flames after the visible flame goes out
pale-blue flames near the limit
smoke particles below 500 nm
words.Where it stops:
lunar or Martian gravity: no data in the PSI repository
solids in the console: no test point above 31.9% oxygen
CO2 with helium: in no FLEX test
words.Last line: Every number in this deck is in the console, with its source.
